rows.recipient: Oklahoma State University Center for Health Sciences (OSU-CHS) – SPARK Rural Health Addiction Medicine Expansion Program,
rows.purpose: Service Area: All 75 rural-designated Oklahoma counties.

rows.recipient: Mercy Health Oklahoma Communities – Virtual Substance Use Recovery Program (vSURP),
rows.purpose: Service Area: 37 rural Oklahoma counties, with 44 physical entry points consisting of seven hospitals and 37 clinics. The 13 primary counties are Blaine, Canadian, Carter, Cleveland, Delaware, Garvin, Johnston, Kingfisher, Le Flore, Logan, McClain, Pontotoc, and Sequoyah, with an additional 24 surrounding rural counties served through the program.
Service Area: Adair, Cherokee, Delaware, Mayes, McIntosh, Muskogee, Okmulgee, and Sequoyah counties.

rows.recipient: Central Oklahoma Family Medical Center, Inc.
rows.purpose: Central Oklahoma Family Medical Center, Inc. will utilize a complex care model designed to target and manage chronic diseases through physicians, RNs, CHWs, and other providers. Patients receiving care at COFMC will be screened for cardiovascular disease, chronic lower respiratory disease, diabetes, and stroke prevention/management and will be flagged due to high rates of emergency room visits or primary care appointments, supported by PRAPARE results. The work will be supported by the Azara platform and include in-person appointments, telemedicine, and follow-up via telephone.

rows.county: Cherokee, Delaware, Mayes, Muskogee, Ottawa, Rogers
rows.purpose: Cherokee County Health Services Council will launch the Empowered Living Program of Northeastern Oklahoma (ELP) - a regional chronic disease self-management initiative serving rural and underserved populations across northeastern Oklahoma. The program will create a coordinated six-county network of healthcare providers, community health organizations, and local outreach coordinators to expand access to Chronic Disease Self-Management Education (CDSME) programs. Using evidence-based Self-Management Resource Center (SMRC) models, the initiative will provide virtual workshops focused on diabetes and cardiovascular disease prevention and management, with future expansion to cancer survivorship, stroke recovery, and chronic respiratory disease support.

rows.county: Atoka, Bryan, Choctaw, Coal, Haskell, Hughes, Johnston, Latimer, LeFlore, McCurtain, Pittsburg, Pontotoc, Pushmataha
rows.purpose: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma will launch the Integrated Rural Chronic Disease Access, Prevention, and Care Coordination Initiative: a system-wide program designed to improve chronic disease management, preventive wellness engagement, and maternal health coordination across rural Southeastern Oklahoma. The program expands access to Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM), digital health engagement tools, preventive wellness services, maternal care coordination, and community-based outreach activities designed to reduce barriers to care and strengthen patient engagement.

rows.recipient: Cimarron Memorial Hospital and Rural Health Clinic
rows.purpose: Cimarron Memorial Hospital and Rural Health Clinic will implement the Frontier Chronic Disease Early Detection and Diagnostic Access Initiative to improve access to evidence-based chronic disease diagnosis, monitoring, and early detection services for residents of Cimarron County and the surrounding frontier region.

rows.county: Caddo, Comanche, Cotton, Jefferson, Stephens, Tillman
rows.purpose: The Comanche Nation will expand its long-standing, community-based chronic disease management services for rural tribal members in southwestern Oklahoma. The initiative will stabilize and expand care by strengthening staff capacity, adding two CHR Transporter/Aides, and introducing a mobile health unit to reach remote communities. Through in-home visits, transportation support, medication delivery, and culturally grounded health education, the program will improve access to care, enhance chronic disease management, and reduce health disparities among American Indian populations in rural areas.

rows.county: Blaine, Dewey, Garfield, Kingfisher, Major, Woods, Woodward
rows.purpose: Fairview Regional Medical Center (FRMC) will launch the Northwest Oklahoma Stroke and Cardiovascular Disease Management Program, a comprehensive initiative designed to improve prevention, diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and long-term management of cardiovascular disease and stroke throughout rural northwest Oklahoma. The project will strengthen care across the continuum through implementation of a population health management platform, care coordination services, advanced diagnostic capabilities, emergency response enhancements, rehabilitation expansion, and chronic disease management.

rows.recipient: Genesis Medical PLLC, dba Southern Oklahoma Pain Management
rows.county: Atoka, Bryan, Carter, Coal, Garvin, Johnston, Marshall, Murray, Pontotoc, Stephens
rows.purpose: Genesis Medical PLLC, dba Southern Oklahoma Pain Management (SOPM), will implement the Southern Oklahoma Rural Chronic Disease Management Program — a structured, multi-condition care management initiative serving patients across 10 rural counties in south-central Oklahoma. SOPM will deploy an evidence-based care management model targeting Type 2 Diabetes, cardiovascular disease and hypertension, and COPD. Program components include proactive patient outreach and enrollment, individualized care plan development and maintenance, monthly patient engagement, closed-loop referral tracking, remote physiologic monitoring, care gap closure, social determinants of health navigation, and structured patient education.

JCMH will implement the Chronic Care Model (CCM) to improve access, quality of care and outcomes of chronic disease for people with chronic respiratory diseases including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), chronic bronchitis, emphysema and asthma. JCMH is the primary inpatient and emergency care facility for Jackson and four neighboring counties. Patients with chronic respiratory diseases rely on immediate access, close to home, to updated technology and immediate and effective treatment for exacerbations of their conditions. The program will address this need for a comprehensive chronic care management program with robust capacity and reach to enable access to chronic disease care close to home for rural residents.

rows.county: Bryan, Carter, Garvin, Johnston, Love, Marshall, Murray, Pontotoc, Seminole
rows.purpose: Lighthouse Behavioral Wellness Centers, Inc. (Lighthouse) will implement the Rural Integrated Lifestyle Medicine and Chronic Disease Pathway Program (RILM-CDP) across its nine-county rural service area. The project will develop and implement standardized, evidence-informed clinical pathways that strengthen chronic disease risk identification, care coordination, referral management, follow-up support, and performance monitoring for individuals receiving behavioral health services who are living with, at risk for, or experiencing barriers to managing diabetes, cardiovascular disease and hypertension, chronic respiratory disease, and stroke-related conditions.

rows.county: Atoka, Carter, Johnston, McCurtain, Murray, Pittsburg, Seminole
rows.purpose: Long Term Care Specialists, Inc. will implement a comprehensive Cardiovascular Program to improve outcomes for residents of 18 rural long-term care and skilled nursing facilities in southeastern Oklahoma. The program combines evidence-based cardiovascular clinical pathways, remote patient monitoring, telecardiology services, point-of-care diagnostics, advanced vascular access capabilities, and integrated care coordination to provide proactive, facility-based management of chronic cardiovascular conditions.

rows.county: Blaine, Carter, Delaware, Garvin, Kingfisher, LeFlore, Logan, Pontotoc, Sequoyah
rows.purpose: MHOC’s will expand its virtual capabilities in rural primary care clinics in accordance with the virtual patient care (VPC) chronic disease optimization model. The proposed project will support a network of 15 rural primary care clinics spanning nine counties across central, south central, and eastern Oklahoma. MHOC will provide 24/7 access to same-day acute care video visits. MHOC will expand access to its virtual chronic condition management team with an initial focus on Medicare-eligible patients.

rows.recipient: Midwest Wellness and Wound Care, LLC
rows.county: 75 rural counties (excluding Oklahoma and Tulsa Counties)
rows.purpose: Midwest Rural Chronic Care Connect (RC3) is a telehealth-enabled chronic disease management program serving rural Oklahoma statewide. Operating a centralized care-coordination and telehealth hub, RC3 uses a dual model: for the many rural patients with no established medical home, RC3 connects them to primary care; for patients who already have a PCP or psychiatrist, RC3 coordinates with that provider. RC3 deploys evidence-based interventions — self-measured blood pressure monitoring (Million Hearts), Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES), spirometry- guided COPD/asthma management (GOLD/NHLBI), and the Collaborative Care Model for co- occurring depression and anxiety, in addition to cellular-connected remote monitoring devices.

rows.county: Bryan, Carter, Garvin, Jefferson, Johnston, Love, Marshall, Murray, Stephens
rows.purpose: Urology Center of Southern Oklahoma will expand its Rural Urologic Cancer and Chronic Disease Management Program to improve timely access to cancer evaluation, diagnosis, treatment coordination, and long-term surveillance for rural patients across Southern Oklahoma. The program will support chronic urologic disease management for conditions that often overlap with or complicate cancer care, reduce referral backlogs, improve cancer care coordination, support telehealth for elderly and transportation-limited patients, and allow more rural patients to receive high-quality urologic cancer care close to home.

rows.recipient: Wagoner Hospital Authority, an Oklahoma Public Trust, DBA Wagoner Community Hospital
rows.county: Adair, Cherokee, Delaware, Muskogee, Okmulgee, Wagoner
rows.purpose: Wagoner Community Hospital will employ the Identify–Equip–Monitor–Rehabilitate–Extend model for chronic disease management. They will identify patients and conduct care coordination through their existing staff and EHR, modernize their clinical infrastructure, launch a patient monitoring program and two rehabilitation programs: pulmonary and post-stroke, and expand access to telehealth for rural patients.

rows.county: Craig, Delaware, Mayes, Muskogee, Nowata, Okfuskee, Osage, Ottawa, Rogers, Wagoner, Washington
rows.purpose: Wyandotte Nation will expand its established diabetes management and prevention program for eligible patients in eleven rural northeastern Oklahoma counties. The project will increase access to diabetes and pre-diabetes education, nutrition instruction, healthy cooking classes, diabetic eye pressure screening, retinal screening, diabetic foot screening, routine monitoring, laboratory review, diabetic follow-up, and healthcare support for patients managing diabetes, pre-diabetes, and related chronic conditions.

Cohort 1 participants: Memorial Hospital of Texas County Authority, Great Plains Regional Medical Center, Beaver County Memorial Hospital, Harper County Community Hospital, DHR Duncan Regional, Okeene Municipal Hospital and Schallmo Authority

CREOKS will invest in two transportation vans for its Stilwell clinic. These vans will directly address barriers to rural transportation and help clients reach behavioral health, medical, wellness, and other supportive services more reliably.

Great Salt Plains Health Center will invest in a new digital X-ray machine to provide clearer, higher-quality images, enabling medical provider teams to diagnose conditions faster and with greater accuracy. Improving imaging quality is a top priority as it improves overall patient health, decreases hospital admissions, reduces the burden on emergency rooms, and leads to quicker referrals to specialists for advanced care.

Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma will invest in vision, hearing, and wellness screening technology, in addition to a vaccine refrigerator and medical privacy tents. These investments directly support the project’s goal of delivering accessible, high-quality health screenings and ensuring safe immunization delivery.

Beaver County Memorial Hospital will invest in new health and wellness equipment to create an exercise space to support and allow employees, their families, and others to work towards a healthier lifestyle. The awardee will also expand its physical therapy department by purchasing specialized equipment for rehabilitation use for all patients in need.
Great Salt Plains Health Center will invest in a vaccine management system to improve vaccine storage, guarantee temperature control, and enhance patient safety.

Bryan County EMS will invest in updated, modern communications equipment to better serve its community. This equipment will be helpful in daily EMS operations, crucial in disasters, and prospectively important in upcoming programs like their “treatment in place” (TIP) initiative.

Avem Health Partners will invest in the purchase and installation of a full outdoor basketball court at Rotary Park. This includes site preparation, concrete installation, goals, surfacing, and necessary safety features to create a functional and durable recreational space. This investment directly addresses the identified gap in safe and accessible opportunities for physical activity in an underserved area of the community.

Southern Oklahoma Ambulance Services will invest in two cardiac monitors and two portable ventilators. Together, these investments equip each additional ambulance with the life‑saving technology necessary to maintain clinical readiness and meet the growing demands of its service area.

rows.recipient: Choctaw County City of Hugo Hospital Authority
rows.purpose: Choctaw County City of Hugo Hospital Authority will invest in four defibrillators, five rechargeable battery packs, and a charger for the batteries. These investments ensure that high-risk patients have immediate access to reliable defibrillation, while healthcare staff have standardized, easy-to-use equipment that meets FDA safety and effectiveness standards.

rows.recipient: Cimarron Memorial Hospital and Rural Health Clinic
rows.purpose: Cimarron Memorial Hospital and Rural Health Clinic will invest in essential equipment required to establish and operate a safe, effective, and fully functional cardiac rehabilitation program. These investments include a recumbent bike and ergometer, cardiac rehabilitation exercise equipment system, a defibrillator, and a wireless stress system.

Absentee Shawnee Tribal Health System will invest in blood pressure cuffs in multiple sizes, glucose monitors, and smart glass body weight scales with BMI indicators. Diagnostic tools help patients track their health progress at home, leading to earlier detection and better management of chronic conditions like diabetes and hypertension. [ER1.1][CP1.2]Investments will also include health and wellness equipment for their diet and wellness programming and rehabilitation.

rows.recipient: Family Health Center of Southern Oklahoma
rows.purpose: Family Health Center of Southern Oklahoma (FHCSO) will invest in home-monitoring equipment, which includes pulse oximeters, digital thermometers, blood pressure cuffs, and scales, to support patients diagnosed with chronic conditions in monitoring key health indicators at home. FHCSO will also invest in a body composition machine to assess overall patient health, including weight, body fat percentage, muscle mass, and fluid balance.

Comanche County Hospital Authority will invest in clinical access infrastructure equipment to deliver point-of-service [BC2.1][ER2.2][CP2.3]care to patients of FQHC clinics in Comanche, County. [BC3.1]CCHA will upgrade X-ray equipment to reduce radiation exposure and deliver faster results via on-the-spot diagnosis, improving patient outcomes, and quality of life.

DRH Health will invest in clinical access and point-of-care equipment for its Rural Health Clinics [ER4.1][CP4.2]to enable providers to conduct medical examinations, diagnose and treat patients, maintain compliance with CMS requirements for Medicare and Medicaid patients, and better support people with disabilities. Equipment includes examination tables, vital signs devices, hypertension management tools, wheelchair accessible scales, education materials to empower patients to manage their chronic conditions, bariatric wheelchairs, and diagnostic equipment.
Baptist Healthcare will invest in one additional ultrasound machine for its clinic. The new system will expand capacity for imaging and improve the overall quality and timeliness of care.

CREOKS will invest in mobile medical carts, a medication dispensing machine, emergency medical cots, laptops, and a transportation van. These investments will strengthen crisis stabilization capacity, improve medication management and emergency readiness, support clinical assessment and workflow, and help clients access needed care and recovery services.

TheraWest LLC will invest in one anti-gravity treadmill, which utilizes NASA-developed differential air-pressure technology to reduce a patient's effective body weight by up to 80%. The technology allows for therapeutic [BC5.1]movement that would otherwise be impossible or painful during the early stages of recovery.

St. Francis Health System will invest in retina scanning and remote patient monitoring equipment. This investment will bring the medical expertise and capacity of the larger Saint Francis Health System network into rural facilities via telemedicine and related equipment, improving the timeliness of specialized treatment and reducing the transportation burden on patients and their families.

Seiling Municipal Hospital will invest in a non-contact, low-frequency ultrasound treatment that promotes wound healing by increasing blood flow, reducing bacteria, and stimulating tissue regeneration. It is particularly beneficial for patients with chronic or complex wounds, including diabetic ulcers, pressure injuries, and post-surgical wounds.

Newman Memorial Hospital, Inc. will invest in new equipment to strengthen diagnostic, respiratory, medication administration, and patient care capacity. Equipment includes IV pumps and a laboratory microscope to ensure continued reliability and accuracy in medication administration and diagnostic testing; a non-invasive ventilator to expand respiratory support capacity during periods of high patient volume; and a bariatric standing scale to improve patient safety and allow for accurate assessment of a broader patient population.

Great Salt Plains Health Center will invest in architectural and engineering (A&E) design services for the repurposing of existing space within the clinical facility to support the expansion of the rural residency teaching program to accommodate up to 12 residents. Services will include facility planning, schematic design, and coordination necessary to reconfigure existing space for clinical and educational use.

Lindsay Municipal Hospital will invest in upgrading and replacing critical equipment to deliver safe, timely, and reliable care in a rural healthcare setting. These investments will support community wellness by improving emergency readiness, enhancing patient safety, and increasing operational efficiency across multiple departments. Equipment includes thermometers, analyzers, a tube rocker, a system for surgical instrument reprocessing, a patient lift, a stretcher, and materials to improve laboratory diagnostic accuracy and efficiency.

Grady Memorial Hospital Authority will invest in a workstation equipped with digital radiography equipment to upgrade to full digital imaging capability, in addition to required preventive maintenance to comply with existing equipment.
Great Salt Plains Health Center will invest in a vaccine management system to improve vaccine storage, guarantee temperature control, and enhance patient safety.

Jackson County Memorial Hospital Authority will invest in clinical access and point-of-care equipment for its Rural Health Clinics [ER8.1][CP8.2]to enable providers to conduct medical examinations, diagnose and treat patients, maintain compliance with HHS requirements for treatment of Medicare and Medicaid patients, and serve people with disabilities. Equipment includes examination tables, a lab draw chair, scopes for conducting examinations, point-of-care ultrasound equipment, and bariatric patient chairs.

Harper County Community Hospital will invest in a pulmonary function test machine to strengthen the hospital's ability to provide comprehensive respiratory care, improve diagnostic capabilities, and enhance overall patient service delivery in the community. Additionally, they will invest in a balance system to strengthen the hospital's rehabilitation services, improve patient safety by addressing fall risk, and expand access to advanced therapeutic technology.

Pafford Medical Services will invest in three categories of advanced prehospital clinical equipment for ambulances. This equipment includes a mechanical chest compression system to deliver automated, consistent chest compressions, an IV pump, and a kit to display a real-time glottis image on an integrated screen.

The City of Wetumka will invest in the development of an active living course to promote healthy lifestyles and encourage regular physical activity for the residents of Wetumka and surrounding communities, in partnership with local organizations. The adult physical fitness equipment is designed to accommodate a range of abilities, including individuals with disabilities, and a protective awning will provide shade and shelter. The City of Wetumka will also invest in walking path signs with designated mileage points to assist users in tracking their activity.

Altus Public Schools will invest in updated, shared-use wellness and strength-training equipment to expand safe, structured physical activity opportunities for students in grades 6–12. Purchases include strength and resistance equipment (such as dumbbells, plates, and benches), cardiovascular equipment (including stationary bikes), and functional training equipment (such as plyometric boxes, medicine balls, and agility tools). The project also includes mobility and recovery equipment (such as resistance bands and suspension trainers), performance monitoring tools to support safe progression, and safety and infrastructure improvements, including flooring, storage systems, and instructional signage.

DRH Health will invest in clinical access and point-of-care equipment for its Rural Health Clinics[ER10.1][CP10.2] to enable providers to conduct medical examinations, diagnose and treat patients, maintain compliance with CMS requirements for Medicare and Medicaid patients, and better support people with disabilities. Equipment includes examination tables, vital signs devices, hypertension management tools, wheelchair accessible scales, education materials to empower patients to manage their chronic conditions, bariatric wheelchairs, and diagnostic equipment.

Mercy Hospital Oklahoma Communities will invest in modern, energy-efficient LED lighting throughout the rural hospital and a modern floor scrubber to strengthen environmental cleanliness and infection control. Additionally, the installation of updated pharmacy storage will improve medication safety, organization, and regulatory compliance within the rural hospital.
Fairfax Medical Facilities, Inc. will invest in equipment to conduct bone mineral density diagnostic testing.

rows.recipient: Great Plains Youth and Family Services, Inc.
rows.purpose: Great Plains Youth and Family Services, Inc. will invest in basic hygiene and dental care items, including toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant, body wash, and shampoo. These items are critical to ensuring children maintain proper personal hygiene, which is closely linked to physical health, self-esteem, and school readiness. Additionally, they will invest in backpacks and age-appropriate school supplies to help ensure students begin the school year equipped, confident, and prepared to learn, and a portion of the funds will be dedicated to promoting early literacy and learning opportunities.

rows.recipient: The LeFlore County Hospital Authority, dba Eastern Oklahoma Medical Center (EOMC)
rows.purpose: The LeFlore County Hospital Authority, dba Eastern Oklahoma Medical Center (EOMC), will invest in a machine with VO2 monitoring for bone density screenings. EOMC will also incorporate infusion services to include osteoporosis therapies, implement a structured fall prevention program, and enhance care coordination through screening referrals, treatment tracking, and patient follow-up.

The Community Market of Pottawatomie County will invest in a 16-foot box truck with an enclosed cargo area, designed for high-capacity transport and mobile delivery of food, supplies, and community resources. Additionally, CMPC will invest in an additional pallet jack, two new tablets, and additional folding tables to manage the increased level of service being provided.

Guthrie Fire EMS will invest in two cardiac monitor/defibrillators and two ventilators to fulfill a documented operational and clinical need by improving equipment availability for a rural EMS system. Dependable monitoring and ventilatory support are essential for safe patient care during response and transport.

Fairview Regional Medical Center will invest in laptops to support mobile care coordination, patient engagement, and community-based education, along with a portable X-ray machine to expand access to diagnostic imaging services in non-traditional and community-based settings.

rows.recipient: Marshall County HMA, dba AllianceHealth Madill
rows.purpose: Marshall County HMA, dba AllianceHealth Madill will invest in one pulmonary function testing (PFT) machine and two pieces of cardiovascular rehabilitation equipment to support the prevention, early detection, and management of chronic heart and lung disease. These investments create a more complete continuum of care, linking diagnosis with recovery and prevention services.

Grand Lake Mental Health will invest in three kiosks in the waiting room of their outpatient clinic to make intake, assessment, and check-in processes less cumbersome and time-consuming for clients. They will also invest in a redesign of nine youth therapy rooms at outpatient clinics, making them more welcoming, trauma-informed, child-friendly, and equipped with therapeutic toys and activities.

Purcell Municipal Hospital will invest in two scopes with cameras, one adult and one pediatric, that will provide high-definition visualization with advanced technologies, enabling clinicians to detect subtle mucosal and vascular abnormalities, supporting an earlier and more accurate diagnosis.

LIFT Community Action Agency, Inc. will invest in commercial-grade fitness equipment, including cardio machines, strength training equipment, flooring, lockers, and essential gym accessories. This investment will provide physical space for residents to use accessible and quality fitness equipment with a focus on low-income individuals and families, adults experiencing stress, anxiety, or depression, and residents with limited access to fitness facilities.

As a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), Stigler HWC places a strong emphasis on supporting individuals and families whose incomes are at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, as well as those who are un/underinsured. Works Wonderfully Foundation will invest in clinical diagnostic equipment, as well as therapeutic equipment that can serve a dual purpose of wellness enablers for community use outside of clinical practice. The investment is part of Project GO!, which seeks to improve health and wellness outcomes among pediatric patients with disabilities.

Avem Health Partners will invest in the purchase and installation of outdoor exercise equipment at Ben Parker Memorial Trail Park. This includes multiple pieces of durable, weather-resistant fitness equipment designed to support strength, cardiovascular health, and flexibility for users of varying ages and ability levels, as well as installation and site preparation. Long Term Care Specialists, Inc. will invest in an ultrasound system to support real-time, image-guided vascular access, which allows trained personnel to more accurately and efficiently place peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs), central venous catheters, IV lines, and other vascular access devices. Each unit is portable and designed for use in facility-based care settings, allowing it to be deployed across multiple branch locations within the county.

rows.recipient: The Clinic at Central Oklahoma Family Medical
rows.purpose: The Clinic at Central Oklahoma Family Medical will invest in a one-exam-room mobile medical clinic to directly address barriers to patient transportation. The Clinic will station the unit across its rural service area to expand access to medical care and encourage uptake of initial and follow-up medical appointments to address and decrease chronic conditions.

SSM Health St. Anthony Shawnee will invest in equipment for telestroke services to address a life-altering and potentially fatal gap in care. The equipment will help to sustain high-volume, around-the-clock consultation at scale.

Clayton Public Schools will invest in telemedicine carts and personal telehealth solutions for five locations in the communities of Clayton, Albion, Tuskahoma, and Nashoba. These locations will provide access points for rural residents to make use of health care and mental health care services.

rows.purpose: Memorial Hospital of Texas County Authority will invest in new and updated physical therapy equipment to improve patient outcomes. The investment will introduce new treatment options for more members of the community and add updated safety features that reduce the risk for both the patient and the therapist.

rows.purpose: Tillman County Emergency Medical Services District will invest in ventilators, IV pumps, and equipment to help start IVs more reliably. The ventilators and IV pumps will enable better management of acutely ill patients and will also support future treatment-in-place (TIP) work.

Wagoner Hospital will invest in replacement psychiatric-rated patient beds for their Mental Health Unit. These specialized safety beds are designed for behavioral health settings, featuring anti-ligature design, low-height fall prevention, tamper-resistant hardware, and infection-resistant surfaces.

Washington County Eldercare will invest in a combination of advanced assessment systems, therapeutic equipment, and program supplies that directly support fall prevention, mobility improvement, and the ability of older adults to maintain their independence. A significant portion of the investment focuses on evidence-based assessment and intervention systems designed to identify and address fall risk.

rows.recipient: Alva Hospital Authority, dba Share Medical Center
rows.purpose: Alva Hospital Authority, dba Share Medical Center, in collaboration with Alva EMS and Survival Flight, will invest in identified equipment that can ease the transition of care between their services in critical and emergent situations. This investment in improved equipment and increased training will improve healthcare outcomes for anyone experiencing a medical emergency in their rural community.

Newman Memorial Hospital, Inc. will invest in equipment across the Woodward Rural Health Clinic, Woodward Specialty Clinic, and Mooreland Clinic to address increased patient volume, improve workflow efficiency, and support the expansion of diagnostic, procedural, and patient care services. rows.recipient: Board of Regents of the University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center,
rows.purpose: Oklahoma Breastfeeding Resource Center

Newman Memorial Hospital will establish the Rural Oklahoma Doula Workforce Development Program in Ellis County with support to Woodward County. The program is a comprehensive hybrid training initiative designed to recruit, educate, certify, mentor, and retain community-based doulas who will improve maternal and infant health outcomes in underserved rural Oklahoma communities. Newman Memorial Hospital seeks to increase the availability of trained doulas serving rural Oklahoma, expand access to labor support for Medicaid beneficiaries, increase breastfeeding initiation, improve patient satisfaction, reduce unnecessary cesarean births, and improve maternal and infant health outcomes.

Parent education includes expanding doula care and education to expecting families through partnerships, education, collaboration, and outreach. Provider education includes expanding doula care and education to professionals such as health providers, students, future doulas, and support staff through partnerships, education, collaboration, and outreach.

rows.recipient: Central Oklahoma Family Medical Center, Inc.
rows.purpose: Central Oklahoma Family Medical Center, Inc. will utilize a complex care model designed to target and manage chronic diseases through physicians, RNs, CHWs, and other providers. Patients receiving care at COFMC will be screened for cardiovascular disease, chronic lower respiratory disease, diabetes, and stroke prevention/management and will be flagged due to high rates of emergency room visits or primary care appointments, supported by PRAPARE results. The work will be supported by the Azara platform and include in-person appointments, telemedicine, and follow-up via telephone.

rows.county: Cherokee, Delaware, Mayes, Muskogee, Ottawa, Rogers
rows.purpose: Cherokee County Health Services Council will launch the Empowered Living Program of Northeastern Oklahoma (ELP) - a regional chronic disease self-management initiative serving rural and underserved populations across northeastern Oklahoma. The program will create a coordinated six-county network of healthcare providers, community health organizations, and local outreach coordinators to expand access to Chronic Disease Self-Management Education (CDSME) programs. Using evidence-based Self-Management Resource Center (SMRC) models, the initiative will provide virtual workshops focused on diabetes and cardiovascular disease prevention and management, with future expansion to cancer survivorship, stroke recovery, and chronic respiratory disease support.

rows.county: Atoka, Bryan, Choctaw, Coal, Haskell, Hughes, Johnson, Latimer, LeFlore, McCurtain, Pittsburg, Pontotoc, Pushmataha
rows.purpose: Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma will launch the Integrated Rural Chronic Disease Access, Prevention, and Care Coordination Initiative: a system-wide program designed to improve chronic disease management, preventive wellness engagement, and maternal health coordination across rural Southeastern Oklahoma. The program expands access to Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM), digital health engagement tools, preventive wellness services, maternal care coordination, and community-based outreach activities designed to reduce barriers to care and strengthen patient engagement.

rows.county: Caddo, Comanche, Cotton, Jefferson, Stephens, Tillman
rows.purpose: The Comanche Nation will expand its long-standing, community-based chronic disease management services for rural tribal members in southwestern Oklahoma. The initiative will stabilize and expand care by strengthening staff capacity, adding two CHR Transporter/Aides, and introducing a mobile health unit to reach remote communities. Through in-home visits, transportation support, medication delivery, and culturally grounded health education, the program will improve access to care, enhance chronic disease management, and reduce health disparities among American Indian populations in rural areas.

rows.county: Blaine, Dewey, Garfield, Kingfisher, Major, Woods, Woodward
rows.purpose: Fairview Regional Medical Center (FRMC) will launch the Northwest Oklahoma Stroke and Cardiovascular Disease Management Program, a comprehensive initiative designed to improve prevention, diagnosis, treatment, rehabilitation, and long-term management of cardiovascular disease and stroke throughout rural northwest Oklahoma. The project will strengthen care across the continuum through implementation of a population health management platform, care coordination services, advanced diagnostic capabilities, emergency response enhancements, rehabilitation expansion, and chronic disease management.

rows.recipient: Genesis Medical PLLC, dba Southern Oklahoma Pain Management
rows.county: Atoka, Bryan, Carter, Coal, Garvin, Johnston, Marshall, Murray, Pontotoc, Stephens
rows.purpose: Genesis Medical PLLC, dba Southern Oklahoma Pain Management (SOPM), will implement the Southern Oklahoma Rural Chronic Disease Management Program — a structured, multi-condition care management initiative serving patients across 10 rural counties in south-central Oklahoma. SOPM will deploy an evidence-based care management model targeting Type 2 Diabetes, cardiovascular disease and hypertension, and COPD. Program components include proactive patient outreach and enrollment, individualized care plan development and maintenance, monthly patient engagement, closed-loop referral tracking, remote physiologic monitoring, care gap closure, social determinants of health navigation, and structured patient education.

JCMH will implement the Chronic Care Model (CCM) to improve access, quality of care and outcomes of chronic disease for people with chronic respiratory diseases including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), chronic bronchitis, emphysema and asthma. JCMH is the primary inpatient and emergency care facility for Jackson and four neighboring counties. Patients with chronic respiratory diseases rely on immediate access, close to home, to updated technology and immediate and effective treatment for exacerbations of their conditions. The program will address this need for a comprehensive chronic care management program with robust capacity and reach to enable access to chronic disease care close to home for rural residents.

rows.county: Bryan, Carter, Garvin, Johnston, Love, Marshall, Murray, Pontotoc, Seminole
rows.purpose: Lighthouse Behavioral Wellness Centers, Inc. (Lighthouse) will implement the Rural Integrated Lifestyle Medicine and Chronic Disease Pathway Program (RILM-CDP) across its nine-county rural service area. The project will develop and implement standardized, evidence-informed clinical pathways that strengthen chronic disease risk identification, care coordination, referral management, follow-up support, and performance monitoring for individuals receiving behavioral health services who are living with, at risk for, or experiencing barriers to managing diabetes, cardiovascular disease and hypertension, chronic respiratory disease, and stroke-related conditions.

rows.county: Atoka, Carter, Johnston, McCurtain, Murray, Pittsburg, Seminole
rows.purpose: Long Term Care Specialists, Inc. will implement a comprehensive Cardiovascular Program to improve outcomes for residents of 18 rural long-term care and skilled nursing facilities in southeastern Oklahoma. The program combines evidence-based cardiovascular clinical pathways, remote patient monitoring, telecardiology services, point-of-care diagnostics, advanced vascular access capabilities, and integrated care coordination to provide proactive, facility-based management of chronic cardiovascular conditions.

rows.county: Blaine, Carter, Delaware, Garvin, Kingfisher, LeFlore, Logan, Pontotoc, Sequoyah
rows.purpose: MHOC’s will expand its virtual capabilities in rural primary care clinics in accordance with the virtual patient care (VPC) chronic disease optimization model. The proposed project will support a network of 15 rural primary care clinics spanning nine counties across central, south central, and eastern Oklahoma. MHOC will provide 24/7 access to same-day acute care video visits. MHOC will expand access to its virtual chronic condition management team with an initial focus on Medicare-eligible patients.

rows.recipient: Midwest Wellness and Wound Care, LLC
rows.county: 75 rural counties (excluding Oklahoma and Tulsa Counties)
rows.purpose: Midwest Rural Chronic Care Connect (RC3) is a telehealth-enabled chronic disease management program serving rural Oklahoma statewide. Operating a centralized care-coordination and telehealth hub, RC3 uses a dual model: for the many rural patients with no established medical home, RC3 connects them to primary care; for patients who already have a PCP or psychiatrist, RC3 coordinates with that provider. RC3 deploys evidence-based interventions — self-measured blood pressure monitoring (Million Hearts), Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES), spirometry- guided COPD/asthma management (GOLD/NHLBI), and the Collaborative Care Model for co- occurring depression and anxiety, in addition to cellular-connected remote monitoring devices.

rows.county: Bryan, Carter, Garvin, Jefferson, Johnston, Love, Marshall, Murray, Stephens
rows.purpose: Urology Center of Southern Oklahoma will expand its Rural Urologic Cancer and Chronic Disease Management Program to improve timely access to cancer evaluation, diagnosis, treatment coordination, and long-term surveillance for rural patients across Southern Oklahoma. The program will support chronic urologic disease management for conditions that often overlap with or complicate cancer care, reduce referral backlogs, improve cancer care coordination, support telehealth for elderly and transportation-limited patients, and allow more rural patients to receive high-quality urologic cancer care close to home.

rows.county: Craig, Delaware, Mayes, Muskogee, Nowata, Okfuskee, Osage, Ottawa, Rogers, Wagoner, Washington
rows.purpose: Wyandotte Nation will expand its established diabetes management and prevention program for eligible patients in eleven rural northeastern Oklahoma counties. The project will increase access to diabetes and pre-diabetes education, nutrition instruction, healthy cooking classes, diabetic eye pressure screening, retinal screening, diabetic foot screening, routine monitoring, laboratory review, diabetic follow-up, and healthcare support for patients managing diabetes, pre-diabetes, and related chronic conditions.

rows.recipient: Board of Regents of the University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center,
rows.purpose: Oklahoma Breastfeeding Resource Center

Newman Memorial Hospital will establish the Rural Oklahoma Doula Workforce Development Program in Ellis County with support to Woodward County. The program is a comprehensive hybrid training initiative designed to recruit, educate, certify, mentor, and retain community-based doulas who will improve maternal and infant health outcomes in underserved rural Oklahoma communities. Newman Memorial Hospital seeks to increase the availability of trained doulas serving rural Oklahoma, expand access to labor support for Medicaid beneficiaries, increase breastfeeding initiation, improve patient satisfaction, reduce unnecessary cesarean births, and improve maternal and infant health outcomes.
Fiscal sponsor for Oklahoma Birth Equity Initiative

rows.recipient: Western Plains Youth and Family Services,
rows.county: Beaver, Cimarron, Dewey, Ellis, Harper, Texas, and Woodward
rows.purpose: Western Plains Youth and Family Services will provide doula training, parent education, and provider education in NW Oklahoma. Training includes use of the Blossoming Birth Community Doula Training Curriculum with an in-house trainer to train others in-person. Parent education includes expanding doula care and education to expecting families through partnerships, education, collaboration, and outreach. Provider education includes expanding doula care and education to professionals such as health providers, students, future doulas, and support staff through partnerships, education, collaboration, and outreach.

rows.county: Caddo, Creek, Kay, Osage, Pawnee, Payne, Pottawatomie
rows.purpose: Communities Foundation of Oklahoma is the fiscal sponsor for PAC Birth Crisis Initiative. PAC Birth Crisis Initiative will provide doula training and parent education in seven rural counties. Community-based, in-person (with hybrid option) training will focus on anchor counties (Kay, Creek, Caddo, and Osage) and is 8-modules and 30 hours. Each module builds sequentially toward full spectrum doula competency, and training includes mentorship and preparation to bill Medicaid for doula services. The parent education component is an evidence-based, three-session childbirth education program with a focus on cultural responsiveness, needs of rural Oklahoma families (including Indigenous families) and families with limited health literacy. The classes will be held inside rural hospitals and birth centers whenever possible.
